newsitem.title: USA: Americans not getting enough exercise - study.
newsitem.headline: Americans not getting enough exercise - study.

text.p: Federal health officials said on Thursday that about 53 million adult Americans were physically inactive during their leisure time, including many arthritis patients who could benefit from exercise.

In a survey of 105,853 people, the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) found that 29.4 percent of adults said that during the previous month, they never exercised or engaged in physical activity unless it was required for their job.
People were more likely to engage in activities such as running, calisthenics, golf, gardening or walking for exercise during the summer than in the winter, the CDC said.
The percentage of people surveyed in 1994 who said they had engaged in no leisure-time physical activity was lowest in June, at 24.7 percent. It was highest in January, when it was 35.3 percent.
The CDC said people with arthritis were more likely to be physically inactive, even though research has shown that they can adapt to increased activity without adverse effects.

"Fully 20 percent of adults are affected by arthritis and other rheumatic conditions," CDC epidemiologist Dr. Chad Helmick said. "They have very high rates of no reported leisure-time physical activity."
The CDC said exercise can improve muscle function, cardiorespiratory capacity and physical performance of those with arthritis.

"People with arthritis might have been mistakenly told in the past that they should not engage in physical activity because it might damage their joints," Helmick said. "There's good scientific evidence that's not true, if you're careful about it."
Regular physical activity can reduce the risk of premature death, heart disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, colon cancer, depression and anxiety, the CDC said.
